title: Docs: Correlation (CORR) definition and scoring horizons

what_it_means: CORR is a per-era rank-style correlation, i.e. the same family of statistic as our per-date rank IC; the 1.5 power up-weights the tails (top and bottom names). A CORR of 0.02 is directly comparable in kind (not in data) to an IC of 0.02.

quote: The key takeaway here is that your prediction's distribution does not matter.
relevance_to_suryadhana: Confirms that a rank IC on a 20-day relative-return label is the industry-standard yardstick for a model like ours; our IC 0.04-0.05 is the right unit to compare with Numerai CORR.

what_it_means: Our arithmetic: with multiplier 3, a CORR60 of 0.02 earns 3 x 0.02 = 0.06 = 6% of stake per round from CORR alone (MMC term extra, and can be negative). The legacy note that extreme payouts were only 1-2% per round implies per-round scores are typically a few hundredths of correlation.

relevance_to_suryadhana: Numerai pays real money for correlations of order 0.01-0.03, which shows that IC levels like ours are economically meaningful when breadth and neutralisation are handled by the fund.

what_it_means: Our arithmetic: daily Sharpe 0.381 x sqrt(245) = 5.96 annualised (10th: 4.38), gross of costs. The expected maximum of 2,033 zero-skill entries is about 3.4 SE = 0.44 (Blom approximation, assuming independence), so the winning score is within the range luck alone can produce.
